Who we are

Melotech is revolutionizing media and entertainment. We create art through technology for humans to enjoy. In just 24 months, our work has been heard, watched and loved for over 4 billion minutes worldwide.

Founded by entrepreneur and investor Soheil Mirpour, we are backed by top VCs Cherry Ventures, Speedinvest and GFC, alongside world-class angels from firms such as Spotify, Blackstone and KKR.

 

What you will do

Melotech is scaling fast, and organic reach is one of the engines behind it. As Growth Associate (Intern), you help run that engine end to end: the creators, the formats, the trends and the numbers behind them. This is an organic growth role first, measured on how much reach every hour and every euro brings back. You work directly with our founders, our Growth Manager, product and data team.

Your first job is to turn organic reach into a machine: find the creators and communities that move culture, turn what works into repeatable playbooks, and run more experiments in a week than most teams run in a quarter.

 

On a typical day, your tasks may include:

  • Creator network: finding and briefing creators at scale, from small accounts with loyal audiences to the ones that set trends, and keeping the ones that deliver

  • Trend spotting: catching formats and memes early and moving on them within days, not weeks

  • Experiments: running many cheap tests every week, with clear rules for what wins and what gets killed, and turning the winners into playbooks the team can repeat

  • New channels: finding places where attention is still cheap, from new communities to platforms nobody on the team is using yet

  • Organic and paid together: working with our Growth Manager so organic winners get scaled with paid, and what paid learns feeds back into organic

  • Measurement: knowing which number answers which question, for example what saves and shares tell you that views do not, and what each view really costs

text:
Who we are

Melotech is revolutionizing media and entertainment. We create art through technology for humans to enjoy. In just 24 months, our work has been heard, watched and loved for over 4 billion minutes worldwide.

Founded by entrepreneur and investor Soheil Mirpour, we are backed by top VCs Cherry Ventures, Speedinvest and GFC, alongside world-class angels from firms such as Spotify, Blackstone and KKR.

 

What you will do

Everything we ship runs on data, and the systems that collect, move and store that data need an owner. As Backend Engineer for Data and Orchestration, you take a data platform that grew fast and turn it into one system the whole company can rely on. You keep it running, you keep it clean, and you make it simpler every month. This is not a pure ETL or warehouse role: you work across the pipelines and the backend services they depend on. We will walk you through exactly what we are building as you go through the process. On a typical day, your tasks may include:

  • Data collection: keeping our external data integrations reliable as sources and APIs change

  • Pipelines and storage: owning our event-driven pipelines end to end, from orchestration (Airflow, Dagster or similar) to databases and warehouses, built to survive failures and to keep costs in check

  • Monitoring and reliability: building the monitoring and alerting (Datadog or similar) that keeps our services and integrations healthy, and the checks on freshness, volume, schema and values that catch a wrong number before anyone downstream notices

  • Backend services: working on the production services and APIs our data flows through, including our JavaScript backends

  • Infrastructure and security: owning CI/CD, infrastructure as code and cloud for our data systems, plus access and secrets: who and what can reach which system, including AI tools

  • Simplification: consolidating what grew fast into one documented system, and removing what is no longer needed

  • Working across the team: explaining what the data can and cannot do to non-technical colleagues, and guiding junior engineers as the team grows

 

Who you are

We are looking for an engineer who runs what they build, and builds things that keep running. You have operated real production systems in a small, fast-moving company, and people trust you with them.

Typically, your profile will look like this:

  • Experience: 3 to 10 years of hands-on engineering, most of it in small or fast-growing companies where you owned production systems yourself rather than handing them to a platform team

  • Python and backend: advanced Python, including async code and long-running data jobs, and enough backend experience to work on production services and APIs, including basic JavaScript or TypeScript backends

  • External data: you have kept third party data integrations reliable in production, and you know how to handle rate limits, retries and changes without notice

text:
About CircuitHub

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.

The Role

CircuitHub makes electronics on demand. Engineers upload a circuit board design; we buy the parts, build the board in our own robotic factory and ship it. More and more of that business is now run by AI agents, and we want you to help build them.

These aren't chatbots. Our agents have real jobs:

  • They inspect boards. An agent checks camera images of every panel we build for wrong, rotated or missing parts.

  • They program robots. Agents read datasheets so our pick-and-place machines know how to handle each new part.

  • They watch the factory. They spot stray parts in robot storage, diagnose printer faults and clear stuck machines.

  • They run the back office. They book supplier invoices, chase late orders, explain quotes and triage bugs.

  • They write our code. Most of what our team ships starts in an agent session.

What you'll do

Find a process people still do by hand and automate it end to end: decide what needs judgement and what needs plain code, build the tools, and prove it works before it runs alone. Then make it cheaper, faster and right more often. You'll also improve the platform every agent runs on, and work closely with the people your work serves, from factory operators to finance.

How we build

  • Evals first. An agent earns the right to work alone: blind tests against people's verdicts, shadow runs beside the humans, replays of past decisions. We track accuracy and cost per run, and re-test whenever we change a model, a prompt or the effort level.

  • Agents judge, code writes. Agents return structured answers. Plain code checks them against a second source and makes every change.

  • Classical first, model second. Cheap vision and maths narrow the problem so the model only looks where it matters.

  • Safe by construction. Agents work in sandboxed cloud machines that never hold real credentials, and tool calls are built so a business action can't run twice.

Recent work

  • Image alignment ranks the parts on each board photo. The worst 20% of parts hold about 90% of real defects, so the agent only inspects those. In a blind re-run it caught all 13 defects operators had marked.

title: Software Engineer, Lab Automation
text:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

You'll build work-cell orchestration, instrument drivers, protocol scheduling, error-recovery logic, and monitoring. Physical systems fail in ways pure software doesn't — a plate gets stuck, a liquid handler skips a well, a temperature controller drifts. Your job is to make the system handle all of it gracefully. This is a broad, hands-on role for a strong engineer who wants their code to drive real machines and see it run the same day.

What You'll Do

  • Build orchestration software that coordinates liquid handlers, plate readers, incubators, and robot arms — handling timing dependencies, state, and error recovery.

  • Reverse-engineer and develop instrument drivers and APIs. Each instrument speaks a different protocol (serial, USB, TCP/IP); you work out how it talks and build a clean abstraction over it.

  • Model and execute complex multi-step protocols reliably — a single run can span dozens of steps across multiple instruments.

  • Build error-recovery logic so that when something fails mid-run, the system retries, skips, alerts, or pauses depending on the failure mode.

  • Create monitoring and observability for work-cell health: instrument status, run progress, error rates.

  • Debug across the software–hardware boundary — figuring out whether bad data is a comms, firmware, calibration, or code problem.

  • Work closely with lab automation engineers, the rest of the software team, and the scientists running production.

Stack

TypeScript and Python, Postgres (Supabase), Modal for compute. We control instruments with open-source Python tooling like PyLabRobot and PyHamilton wherever we can, rather than proprietary vendor GUIs.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering skills. You write production code in Python and/or TypeScript — well-structured and maintainable, not just prototypes.

  • Comfortable at the hardware-software boundary. You've built software that drives physical devices, or you're excited to. You can read a protocol spec, debug a flaky connection, and reason about timing.

Gain is the Private Markets Super App, a connected global platform transforming how leading investors, advisors, and corporates source, evaluate, and execute deals.   • Raising the bar in the team through design reviews, pairing, and an eval-first habit that sticks.

title: AI Builder — Working Student
text:
EggAI Labs · Working Student · In Person (Tübingen, Germany)

Designing lifecycle evaluation for nondeterministic domain-specific AI systems.

EggAI Labs

We're opening the EggAI Labs in Tübingen. The Labs purpose is to test new AI capabilities, identify what works, how they'd improve delivery, and then build assets to support teams and clients. EggAI's mission cannot be achieved through one-off client projects alone and the Labs is the way to adapt and scale.

As part of the first cohort, you will join a small peer group and work directly with EggAI's CAIO, a Tübingen alumnus. You will also collaborate with our engineering, product, and project leads, who will bring you insights from client problems, help you understand their context and challenge your solutions for them. Your fellow AI Builders will be deliberately chosen to span different passions and strenghts. You will have room to explore and be expected to turn that exploration into something useful. This is not a client-facing role.

The problem: EvalOps

How do we prove an AI system acts as expected under various conditions?

We will explore EvalOps: the methods and tools used to check whether domain-specific AI systems meet their behavioral requirements. Among the key challenges for operating AI systems are nondeterminism, ground-truth curation, evaluation metric-design, latency and costs. EvalOps need to overcome all of them in a disciplined way.

These questions will guide the initial work:

  • Regression suites: How can domain experts turn traces, code, and prompts into useful evals in a way that scales?

  • Coverage estimation: How can we quantify the gaps between an eval suite and the range of expected agent behaviors?

  • Live monitoring: Is it possible to detect anomalous behaviour in production with a similar precision to regression evals?

  • Eval analysis: How much evidence is enough to act (e.g., deploy, debug, roll back a feature, choose a different model)? You will help refine them, test approaches, create assets, and pose new questions.

The role

As an AI Builder, you will take an open EvalOps problem from investigation to a working prototype, ready to be tested. Whatever your focus, you will be expected to take a problem through to a useful result. Here is what that means in practice:

  • Research emerging AI and evaluation capabilities and distinguish substance from hype.

  • Understand the user, workflow, domain, and organisational problem around the work.

  • Evaluate usefulness, quality, safety, and reliability with appropriate evidence.

  • Communicate decisions and learning clearly.

  • Create assets that other people can understand, use, and improve.

  • Code and build end to end.

This shared foundation leaves room for different strengths and interests. Each AI Builder will then develop greater depth in one of three pillars.

Limatica measures what batteries whisper. We turn the tiny voltage noise of battery cells into a quality verdict, far faster than conventional tests, and help cell manufacturers cut scrap.

We are a team of twelve in Chemnitz and Munich, spanning data, ML, HPC, hardware and industrialization. Early adopters across Europe and Asia already use our technology. In 2026 we move from pilots to production lines, and our data grows faster than our team.

What You'll Do

Our measurement stations produce several hundred GB of high-resolution voltage data per hour. You own the step from raw signal to reliable answer.

  • Work with novel cell noise data: Derive features from raw time series that make physical sense that hold up in production
  • Build for streaming: Design feature computations that work in streaming mode, at a throughput of up to 10,000 measurements per hour.
  • Make throughput a design decision: Build modular, parameterizable nodes for our distributed processing pipeline and help bring them into our Rust-based production environment.
  • Ship modules, not scripts: Automate evaluations end to end, from raw data to reports for our engineering team and our customers.
  • Own customer projects technically: Assess requirements, communicate interim results and findings, and turn feedback into improvements.

text:
About Niantic Spatial

AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time.

That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.

In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.

Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.

About the Role

You'll help build the geometric foundation of the next-generation world map — joining our World Map Research Engineering team (Geospatial Alignment) as a Research Engineer or Senior Research Engineer. You'll develop new algorithms, produce the research data and evaluation assets needed to advance them, and engineer the resulting capabilities into dependable production systems.

The World Map team works with heterogeneous captures from phones and handheld devices, aerial imagery, LiDAR, and 360 cameras, as well as external geographic and elevation data. The central challenge is to harmonize these data sources, quantify uncertainty, and maintain consistency as the map evolves.

You'll work at the intersection of cutting-edge research and scalable engineering — developing new approaches to geospatial registration, correspondence, and geometric optimization, then productionizing these technologies to directly improve Niantic Spatial's world model.

What You'll Do

title: Junior Transformation Strategist (UK Based)
text:
About Duvo

Before Duvo, our founders built and ran a $2 billion retailer. They saw how much critical work still depended on spreadsheets, inboxes, supplier portals and the memory of experienced operators. The real process rarely lived in one system. People held the last mile together.

Duvo is building the Enterprise Execution OS: the shared layer that understands how work really runs, carries it across existing systems and measures the business result.

Our agents do the work, not just suggest the next step. They gather evidence, make decisions within agreed rules, route exceptions to the right person and update the source system. People keep control wherever judgment or approval is needed. Every action leaves an audit trail.

We start with one recurring process and a clear outcome. Every solution carries a contracted 5x ROI guarantee.

The role

As a Junior Transformation Strategist, you are the insight and output engine beside our Transformation Strategists on our largest accounts.

On bigger engagements we need more than technical delivery. We need someone who can take a messy process, find the critical question, get to a clear insight fast, and put it into materials a customer team will act on. Today that work often lands on Forward Deployed Engineers. That is the wrong use of a scarce technical resource. This role exists so that insight work has a dedicated owner.

You will work alongside Transformation Strategists (who own day-to-day account presence and workstream direction) and Forward Deployed Engineers (who own the technical solution). You do not own the executive relationship or the commercial outcome. You own the speed and quality of the analytical and written work that makes those conversations possible.

This is a fungible problem-solving role. You will be thrown at different accounts and different problem types (category, supply chain, finance ops, inventory, commercial) and expected to produce. Ideal for someone currently ~2–4 years into a client-facing career as an Associate, Senior Associate, or Consultant at McKinsey or BCG who wants concentrated ownership, not another staffing cycle.

We want to hire two people into this role quickly.

What you will do

1. Get to the insight

  • Dive into how work actually happens: interviews, extracts, handoffs, exceptions and the workarounds people use to keep things running.

  • Build a fact base that shows where cost, cash, service, cycle time or control is being lost.

  • Form a hypothesis early, name what would kill it, and pressure-test it with the Transformation Strategist before you polish anything.

  • Structure unfamiliar problems without waiting for a perfect brief. Frame the selection equation (what matters, what does not) so the team and the customer can decide.

2. Deliver output that moves a decision

  • Turn analysis into decision-ready slides, one-pagers and memos that make the important choice obvious.

  • Be exact about baselines, assumptions and evidence. Do not use polish to hide uncertainty.

  • Work fast: same-day or next-day turnarounds on defined asks are the norm, not the exception.

  • Produce materials a Transformation Strategist can take into a working session or steerco with minimal rewrite.

3. Be fungible surge capacity on big accounts

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.

The role

Mechatronics Engineers at CircuitHub own projects end to end. You'll start with a problem, often on our factory floor, and take it all the way to a working machine:

  • Understand the problem and turn it into a clear specification

  • Generate ideas and choose the right mechanism

  • Design it in CAD and prove it out with the engineering calculations

  • Prototype and build it, machining parts in our in-house CNC shop

  • Bring it to life with software on our in-house robotics operating system

We work AI-first. AI tools help you scope the problem, drive your CAD, run the calculations and write the machine software. The software side needs basic software engineering skills, not a software background: you'll write it with AI agents, supported by a dedicated software engineering team who build the operating system.

You must have built things before, ideally robots, whether as a hobbyist, student, employee or founder. We don't hire narrow specialists. We want engineers who can:

  • Work autonomously and communicate clearly with a team spread across sites

  • Take responsibility for how their machines perform in live production

Things you'll do

This is a design role with hands-on prototyping. For example:

  • Conceive new mechanisms to handle electronics parts and other robotic handling tasks, using AI to scope and specify the problem

  • Design gantries and end effectors in Fusion 360

  • Use AI agents to run the engineering calculations, and know when to distrust them

  • Machine prototype parts in our in-house CNC shop

  • Analyse end-effector behaviour from video and revise its geometry and control approach to improve throughput and reliability

  • Program machine behaviour on our in-house robotics operating system, with AI agents doing the heavy lifting

  • Specify sensors that catch errors while a machine is running, or monitor a chemical process

  • Prototype and deploy a new test robot for in-line PCB validation

  • Commission your machines and hand them over to our build team to scale up

title: Technicien CVC Frigoriste Datacenter H/F
text:
MDC RECRUTEMENT, cabinet de recrutement référence dans la filière Datacenter, recherche pour son client, opérateur d’infrastructures de calcul et d’énergie de très forte puissance dédiées à l’intelligence artificielle, un TECHNICIEN CVC FRIGORISTE SENIOR H/F.

Vos missions

Au cœur de salles techniques où l’arrêt n’est pas une option, vous faites tourner la production de froid et de climatisation en lien avec les équipes d’exploitation et de maintenance :

  • Maintenance du froid et du CVC : vous planifiez et réalisez les opérations préventives et les réparations sur les groupes froid, la ventilation, le chauffage et la climatisation.

  • Recherche de pannes : vous remontez à la cause réelle d’une défaillance, vous rétablissez l’équipement et vous évitez qu’elle se reproduise.

  • Réaction sur incident : vous êtes en première ligne quand un événement technique menace le fonctionnement du site, pour maintenir le service sans interruption.

  • Coordination des prestataires : vous accompagnez les entreprises extérieures sur site, vous validez la qualité de leurs interventions et vous veillez au respect des règles de sécurité.

  • Surveillance des équipements : vous effectuez des tournées de contrôle pour repérer les dérives avant qu’elles ne deviennent des pannes.

  • Efficacité énergétique : vous lisez les relevés de fonctionnement, vous suivez les rendements des installations et vous proposez des pistes pour consommer moins.

  • Culture sécurité : vous appliquez les procédures d’exploitation et les standards HSE du site, et vous les faites vivre auprès de vos interlocuteurs.

  • Progrès continu : vous remontez vos idées pour fiabiliser et moderniser le parc.


Le profil recherché
Prérequis :

  • 8 ans d’expérience minimum indispensables en maintenance d’installations CVC ou de froid industriel.

  • Attestation de manipulation des fluides frigorigènes (catégorie I) exigée, ainsi qu’une habilitation électrique (BR, B1/B2 ou équivalent) exigée.

  • Résidence à Grenoble ou à proximité immédiate impérative : seules les personnes déjà installées dans le bassin grenoblois seront étudiées.

Compétences attendues :

  • Maîtrise de la recherche de pannes et de la maintenance sur équipements de production de froid et de CVC.

  • Pratique des bases d’électricité, de régulation ou d’automatisme appliquées au génie climatique.

  • Aisance requise

Votre mission

Dans un environnement où la disponibilité et la fiabilité des infrastructures sont essentielles, Isatalent recherche un(e) Head of DC Operations pour piloter les opérations de ses data centers en région parisienne.

title: Stage - Data Engineer - ML (H/F)
text:
Chez Withings, nous développons des appareils de santé connectée : nos balances connectées, montres hybrides, tensiomètres, moniteurs de sommeil et tous les dispositifs de notre gamme sont aujourd'hui utilisés par des millions d'utilisateurs. Notre objectif est de permettre la prévention, le dépistage et l'accompagnement d'un certain nombre de maladies chroniques via des produits et des services innovants afin de révolutionner la manière dont on prend soin de sa santé.

Au sein de l'équipe Machine Learning, nous développons des algorithmes pour extraire des informations physiologiques et médicales pour nos utilisateurs tels que le SPO2, la fréquence cardiaque, la présence de diverses pathologies comme la fibrillation atriale, l'apnée du sommeil…
Nous recherchons un ou une stagiaire motivé.e par des sujets de santé avec des compétences en traitement du signal, en machine learning et en deep learning pour nous aider à concevoir les algorithmes de demain.

Votre mission
L'objectif de ce stage est de concevoir, développer et valider des algorithmes capables d'extraire des informations physiologiques et médicales fiables à partir des signaux physiques collectés par nos dispositifs.
Pour mener à bien cette mission passionnante, la/le stagiaire aura l'opportunité de :

  • Explorer et analyser des ensembles de données physiologiques réelles issues de nos utilisateurs, à la recherche de marqueurs pertinents.
  • Concevoir et développer des algorithmes combinant des techniques de traitement du signal innovantes, des heuristiques informatiques fines, des approches Machine Learning et Deep Learning (supervisé ou non).
  • Travailler sur l'optimisation algorithmique en vue d'une implémentation embarquée, potentiellement en langage C, sur des systèmes aux ressources contraintes.
  • Participer à la définition des critères de succès et des métriques pour le mesurer, et évaluer la performance des algorithmes sur des jeux de données variés.

Ce stage offre une immersion complète dans le développement d'un produit de santé connecté de pointe, avec une application concrète et un impact direct sur la vie des utilisateurs. Vous rejoindrez une équipe multidisciplinaire et dynamique, où votre contribution sera essentielle pour transformer un prototype algorithmique en une fonctionnalité embarquée de nos dispositifs, conforme aux exigences de fiabilité et de performance de l'industrie médicale.
Le sujet précis sera discuté avec le stagiaire au plus tard quelques semaines avant le stage.

Requirements

  • Connaissances théoriques en traitement du signal et en machine learning
  • Compétences informatiques : programmation en Python, première expérience en framework deep learning (PyTorch ou TensorFlow) appréciée
  • Bonus : programmation en C
  • Intérêt pour le machine learning
  • Intérêt pour les applications en santé connectée
  • Lecture de l'anglais scientifique et technique
  • Capacité rédactionnelle, de rigueur et d'autonomie
  • Aptitude pour le travail en équipe et communication
  • Durée : 4 à 6 mois

Benefits

Rejoindre l’aventure Withings, c’est :

  • Intégrer un des pionniers et leaders mondiaux de la santé connectée, plusieurs fois primé au Consumer Electronic Show
  • Contribuer à des projets innovants et ambitieux pour la santé de demain dans un environnement agile et en constante évolution
  • Intégrer une entreprise internationale, membre de la FrenchTech 120, dont les équipes sont basées à Issy-les-Moulineaux, Boston, Hong-Kong et Shenzhen

title: Test Engineer
text:
Join our cutting-edge start-up adventure!

Who are we?

Join the Revolution in GNSS and IoT Connectivity

At Qualinx, we’re not just building chips, we’re engineering the future fabric of the connected world. As a pioneering semiconductor scale-up, we’re transforming how devices connect, communicate, and operate through our ground-breaking Digital RF technology. Our mission goes beyond ultra-low power GNSS: we’re redefining what’s possible in adaptive, scalable, and intelligent connectivity for the Internet of Things.

Born from deep-tech innovation at TU Delft, our team of visionary engineers and bold thinkers is tackling the toughest challenges in GNSS and IoT, starting with power consumption and expanding into dynamic, context-aware solutions that adapt to any environment or use case. We’ve already achieved what many thought impossible: the world’s most advanced GNSS chipset. But that’s just the beginning.

At Qualinx, we believe that the future of connectivity lies in precision, efficiency, and adaptability. Our ambition is to become the invisible thread that seamlessly interconnects billions of devices: powering a smarter, more responsive world.

What Sets Us Apart

Joining Qualinx is about becoming part of a culture that’s as ambitious as it is authentic. We hold ourselves to high standards, thrive on solving the unexpected, and push boundaries together. But we also know how to enjoy the ride. Our culture is a unique blend of curiosity, team spirit, and a touch of unconventional charm. It’s fast-paced, fun, and grounded in a sober sense of purpose and perspective. Whether we’re deep in design reviews or sharing laughs over lunch, we’re building something meaningful together. At Qualinx, you’re not just contributing to a ground-breaking technology, you’re helping shape a team that’s redefining what it means to work in deep tech.

Job Description 

As a Test Engineer, you will support the development and production release of test solutions for Qualinx products. Working closely with Design, Product Engineering, Reliability, and external manufacturing partners, you will contribute to digital and memory test development activities, product characterization, yield improvement, and production support.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Support the development, validation, and release of production test solutions for Qualinx products.

  • Support in developing and debugging ATE test programs for wafer sort and final test.

  • Support silicon characterization, correlation, and production qualification activities.

  • Analyze test results and production data to identify issues and opportunities for yield improvement.

  • Work with Design and Product Engineering teams to investigate test failures and support root cause analysis.

  • Contribute to test time optimization and test coverage improvements.

  • Support OSAT and manufacturing partners during product bring-up and production ramp.

  • Assist in implementing and validating digital test methodologies, including SCAN, MBIST, JTAG, and Flash testing.

  • Develop automation scripts and tools to improve test efficiency and data analysis.

  • Maintain test documentation and support continuous improvement of test processes.

title: Performance Engineer
text:
UK | Full-Time

The Mission: Source.dev

Our founders spent over a decade at Google shaping the Android operating systems - building and shipping the software that now runs on billions of devices. They didn't just use Android; they led teams responsible for the Android Virtualization Framework, Security, and the Android Runtime (ART).

Through that journey, they saw a quiet but massive crisis: as device software grew in complexity, the tools used to build it remained stuck in the past. Today, a standard Android checkout exceeds 200GB of code, and builds can take hours. This "wait time" is the single biggest tax on innovation.

Source.dev was founded to reimagine software development workflows for device makers. We’re building a new generation of software tools that make building complex device software feel as simple as building a webpage - starting with SourceFS.

The Core Product: SourceFS

SourceFS is a high-performance virtual filesystem designed to turn multi-hour workflows into minutes.

  • 10x Faster Builds: Intelligent caching and virtualization that only materializes files when they are actually needed.

  • 10x Lower Costs: Enabling a standard 16-vCPU machine to outperform even a 128-vCPU machine.

  • True Engineering Productivity: Replaying hundreds of thousands of build steps instantly when inputs match.

The Cultural Anchor: Own It

We operate with a high degree of trust and a shared value of End-to-End Ownership:

"We own our work end-to-end, from spark to finish. It’s about more than just tasks; it’s the dedication to see things through, staying curious to solve problems, thinking from first principles and ensuring we fix our customer’s problems in the best possible way.”

The Role: Pushing the Speed Limits of Rust, Linux & I/O

We are looking for a Performance / Systems Engineer to join us at Source.dev. In this role, your primary metric of success is speed. You will dissect execution paths, eliminate kernel-space context-switching costs, optimize memory layouts, and ensure SourceFS runs as close to the hardware limits as physically possible.

What You’ll Work On

  • System Bottleneck Hunting: Profile, trace, and eliminate latency across CPU, memory, and disk I/O bottlenecks in Rust systems code using tools like perf, eBPF, valgrind, and custom microbenchmarks.

  • Kernel & File System Tuning: Deep dive into Linux kernel interactions, optimizing FUSE drivers, VFS caches, asynchronous I/O (io_uring), memory-mapped execution, and thread scheduling.

  • Memory & Cache Efficiency: Optimize data structures for cache locality, minimize allocation overhead, and eliminate unnecessary memory copies across boundary transitions.

title: Flight Test Instrumentation & Data Engineer
text:
The Flight Test Instrumentation (FTI) & Data Engineer will be responsible for the end-to-end handling, quality assurance, accessibility, and long-term management of all flight data. The primary objective is to ensure that full-aircraft data, from the onboard sensors and DAQ systems to the final processing tools, is available to every engineering team through a reliable, efficient, and standardized workflow.

Tasks

Flight Test Instrumentation (FTI) & DAQ Pipeline

  • Manage the data pipeline from the physical sensor and Data Acquisition (DAQ) level for the full aircraft, ensuring seamless and accurate transmission into the telemetry and storage systems.
  • Maintain sensor configuration, calibration records, and metadata to guarantee the accurate translation of raw physical signals into usable engineering units.
  • Collaborate with hardware, software and integration teams to define sensor requirements, DAQ architectures, scaling, and telemetry bandwidth allocations.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve data anomalies at the DAQ and sensor level (e.g., signal noise, dropouts, faulty scaling) before they propagate into downstream databases.

Data Infrastructure & Accessibility

  • Maintain reliable extraction of flight data from InfluxDB.
  • Develop and maintain standardized local data structures for analysis, plotting, and visualization.
  • Optimize access to large flight datasets while minimizing CPU and memory usage.
  • Design and maintain an efficient local storage solution for processed flight data.
  • Support future improvements to the flight data architecture as storage requirements, sensor counts, and analysis needs continue to evolve.

Data Quality & Analysis Support

  • Maintain derived datasets to ensure common calculations and signals are shared consistently across teams.
  • Ensure strict timing synchronization and timestamp accuracy across all recorded data, from the sensor acquisition point to the database.
  • Monitor data quality, completeness, and integrity throughout the entire pipeline.
  • Provide fast data previews for rapid post-flight reviews.
  • Enable efficient access to high-frequency sensor data for detailed engineering investigations.
  • Support custom querying of processed datasets.

Requirements

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Data Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • 3+ years of professional experience in test instrumentation, data acquisition (DAQ), or sensor-to-database time-series data engineering (aerospace, automotive, or racing/motorsports preferred).
  • Hands-on experience working directly with physical aircraft/vehicle sensor installations, DAQ hardware, and telemetry pipelines.

Technical & Domain Expertise

1. Hardware, Sensors & DAQ Architecture

  • Strong understanding of physical sensors (e.g., strain gauges, accelerometers, thermocouples, pressure transducers, RTDs, LVDTs, pitot-static tubes).
  • Demonstrated knowledge of signal conditioning, sampling rate selection, anti-aliasing filtering, scaling, and sensor calibration procedures.

2. Data Infrastructure & Software Development

  • Proficient in Python or MATLAB for data analysis, automated data processing, and visualization library development (e.g., Pandas, NumPy, SciPy).
  • Experience working with time-series databases, specifically InfluxDB (or similar engines), including writing efficient queries (Flux/InfluxQL) and data retrieval pipelines.
  • Solid foundation in data structures and memory/CPU optimization when handling high-memory high-frequency continuous time-series datasets.

title: Software Test Engineer
text:
We are looking for a hands-on Software Test Engineer to ensure the quality and reliability of software solutions used in real-world sensing and data processing systems. 

Optics11 is a deep-tech company developing advanced fiber-optic sensing technologies for challenging environments and applications in energy and underwater security. Our systems enable high-performance sensing and monitoring through advanced photonics, signal processing, and data-driven intelligence.

We are expanding our R&D team with a Software Test Engineer who is passionate about quality, structured validation, and delivering robust software in complex engineering environments. 

As a Software Test Engineer, you will be responsible for defining and executing practical software tests to validate software components (including algorithms, cloud back-end, and user interfaces) that process sensor signals generated by fiber-optic sensing systems. You will work closely with data scientists, signal processing specialists, back-end developers, and software architects to ensure that products meet functional and non-functional requirements.

This role requires a hands-on professional with a proactive mindset, a structured approach to software testing, strong attention to detail, and the ability to understand complex technical systems and translate requirements into effective test strategies.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform functional, integration, regression, system, and end-to-end testing across edge devices, cloud services, APIs, databases, and graphical user interfaces.

  • Define test strategies, test plans, test cases, acceptance criteria, and automated test scripts for an edge and cloud software platforms.

  • Identify, document, and track software defects, ensuring clear reproduction steps and proper follow-up.

  • Collaborate with product owners, developers and engineers to understand system requirements and ensure test coverage.

  • Contribute to the development and maintenance of automated test frameworks and pipelines.

  • Test edge–cloud behaviour under interrupted connectivity, delayed or duplicated messages, device restarts, software updates, and synchronization failures.

  • Validate software performance, reliability, and stability under different operating conditions.

  • Support testing of software running on edge hardware, including hardware–software integration in laboratory and field environments.

  • Analyse test results and provide clear, actionable feedback to development teams.

title: Product System Engineer

title: Stage AI & Automatisering | Amsterdam hbo/wo
text:
Wat ga je doen?

Binnen Flagship Amsterdam zijn we volop bezig om met AI en automatisering ons werk slimmer en makkelijker te maken. Daar kunnen we jouw hulp goed bij gebruiken! Als stagiair AI & Automatisering ben je de rechterhand van de specialist voor IT en automatisering. Je onderzoekt bestaande processen, denkt mee over verbeteringen en helpt bij het ontwikkelen van nieuwe tools. Je krijgt veel ruimte om zelf ideeën uit te werken en leert tijdens deze stage ontzettend veel over AI, technologie en automatisering.

Wat ga je leren?

  • AI en automatisering inzetten in de praktijk;

  • Zelf slimme tools en oplossingen ontwikkelen;

  • Bestaande processen verbeteren en efficiënter maken;

  • Werken met verschillende AI-tools en technologieën;

  • Ervaring opdoen met echte projecten binnen een groeiend bedrijf;

  • Je eigen ideeën uitwerken en veel nieuwe vaardigheden ontwikkelen.

Praktisch

Startdatum: in overleg;

Beschikbaarheid: 3–5 dagen per week, in te richten rond je studierooster;

Locatie: kantoor in hartje Amsterdam;

Stagevergoeding: €500 per maand bij 5 dagen per week.

Dit bieden wij

  • Een uitdagende en leerzame stage waarin je écht meedraait in het team;

  • Intensieve begeleiding door een ervaren IT-specialist, met ruimte voor persoonlijke en professionele ontwikkeling;

  • Een centraal gelegen kantoor op ca. 15 minuten lopen van Amsterdam Centraal;

  • Een gezellige werksfeer en een heerlijke, verzorgde lunch op kantoor;

  • Legendarische vrijdagmiddagborrels, sportieve uitjes en bedrijfsfeesten;

  • 25% personeelskorting op rondvaarten en andere activiteiten binnen Flagship Holding;

  • De mogelijkheid om je stage af te sluiten met een concrete showcase- of portfolio-project.

Functievereisten

  • Je volgt een HBO- of WO-opleiding in bijvoorbeeld AI, ICT, Informatica, Business IT of een vergelijkbare richting;

  • Ervaring met API-koppelingen en databases is mooi meegenomen;

  • Je hebt basiskennis van programmeren en vindt het leuk om hierin verder te leren;

  • Zelfstandig werken gaat je goed af en je neemt graag zelf initiatief;

  • Je kunt goed communiceren in het Engels, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk.


Over Flagship

Flagship Amsterdam is een jonge en snelgroeiende rederij in het hart van Amsterdam. Wat in 2017 begon met drie boten, is inmiddels uitgegroeid tot een vloot van meer dan 70 boten, en we groeien nog steeds elke dag verder! Jaarlijks verwelkomen we gasten uit meer dan 55 verschillende landen, en we varen het hele jaar door. Dit doen we met een gedreven en ambitieus team van meer dan 800 (seizoensgebonden) medewerkers.

Maar Flagship is meer dan alleen rondvaarten. Vanuit dezelfde energie bouwen we aan verschillende concepten die allemaal draaien om beleving, gastvrijheid en de stad Amsterdam. Zo ontdek je de stad op de fiets met Flagship Bike Tours, proef je de sfeer bij Flagship Waffle Experience Amsterdam, en werken we bij Shipyard aan unieke events en creatieve projecten op en rond het water. Daarnaast hebben we labels zoals Voyage Amsterdam, Captain Jack en Aemstelland, elk met hun eigen stijl en doelgroep. Samen vormen ze één organisatie, maar met verschillende manieren om mensen de stad te laten ervaren.

title: Data & AI Consultant
text:
Ben jij de consultant die niet alleen adviseert, maar ook daadwerkelijk de leiding neemt over de uitvoering? Die precies weet hoe een modern data platform eruitziet, welke architectuurkeuzes ertoe doen en hoe je een klant overtuigt om de juiste koers te varen? Dan zoeken wij jou.

Bij BigData Republic bouwen we aan de data- en AI-ambities van toonaangevende organisaties. We zijn AI-native en combineren dit met diepgaande engineering kennis. Op deze manier bieden wij onze klanten technische begeleiding tot duurzame en innovatieve oplossingen. Als Data & AI Consultant ben jij de schakel tussen strategische visie en hands-on realisatie, een rol die we nu voor het eerst toevoegen aan ons team.



Wat ga je doen?

Je werkt bij onze klanten op het snijvlak van strategie en technologie. Je bent geen consultant die alleen analyseert en dat tot slides verwerkt. Jij hebt de regie van A tot Z, van hulpvraag tot en met implementatie. Je analyseert- en vertaalt de wensen van onze partners naar technisch elegante oplossingen, van platform engineering tot MLOps en AI implementatie. Vervolgens begeleid je de teams bij onze klanten die dit in productie brengen.

  • Je vertaalt business-uitdagingen naar concrete data- en AI-strategieën en maakt dit inzichtelijk voor zowel C-level als engineering teams.

  • Je adviseert over data-architecturen, platformen en technologiekeuzes (cloud, lakehouse, real-time, batch) en bent in staat dit inhoudelijk te verdedigen.

  • Je leidt de implementatie: je stuurt data engineers en scientists aan, bewaakt de kwaliteit en houdt de grote lijn in het oog.

  • Je bouwt een vertrouwensrelatie op bij de klant en groeit uit tot een vaste sparringpartner op directieniveau.

  • Je draagt bij aan de inhoudelijke kennisbasis van BigData Republic via interne kennissessies, blogposts of externe presentaties.


Je hebt minimaal 5 jaar ervaring in een data-gerelateerde rol, waarvan minimaal 3 jaar in een consultancy- of leidende positie.

  • Je hebt diepgaande kennis van data-architectuurprincipes: data mesh, lakehouse, streaming vs. batch, governance en datakwaliteit.

  • Je bent thuis op minimaal een van de grote cloudplatformen (Azure, AWS of GCP) en weet welke managed services wanneer worden ingezet.

  • Je snapt hoe moderne AI-toepassingen werken (LLM's, ML-pipelines, MLOps) en weet hoe je ze verantwoord in productie brengt.

  • Je communiceert helder: je maakt complexe technische materie toegankelijk zonder de diepgang te verliezen.
